format: Dealership service invoice - the final bill, with work and money on the same page
why: The document that should win every field when a visit produces a whole stack. It is the only sheet of the five carrying both what was done and what was actually owed.

The correct total, 3,106.49, is independently confirmed by the official receipt for the same visit. That makes this the one case in the set whose totalCost is cross-checked against a second physical document rather than read once.

It prints a JOB DONE block in prose - REPLACED ENGINE OIL, REPLACED ENGINE OIL FILTER, INSPECTED BRAKE PADS AND DISCS, INSPECTED STEERING WHEEL, LINKAGE AND GEAR BOX - separately from the priced line table. Two descriptions of the same visit at different granularity, which is a real chance to double-count operations.

The line table carries << Total for Job 000001 >> and << Total for Job 000002 >> subtotal rows in the middle of the lines. These are sums of the lines above them, and an extractor that treats them as lines will double the money.

Labour bills at 0.00 here against 700.00 on the estimate, because the 1,000 km check-up was free under a maintenance promo. A zero-priced operation is a real line and must not be dropped for having no cost.
kept: shop name, branch, address, phone and VAT TIN

notes: The line amounts reconcile exactly: 0.00 + 210.11 + 38.25 + 1,647.16 = 1,895.52 for job 1, plus 878.13 for job 2 = 2,773.65 Sub Total, plus 332.84 VAT = 3,106.49 TOTAL PRICE.

Reference Repair Order No. G7IA123581 is printed in the header. That is the link that will let a later change group the sheets of one visit together, and it is why referenceNumbers is extracted now rather than after the grouping work.
